blocks.content: Every winter, cities across North India disappear under a thick layer of smog. People blame traffic. Industries. Weather. But one silent contributor continues to dominate headlines — stubble burning, locally known as parali jalana.

As a student living in Delhi, Ayush Paul did not just observe the problem. He decided to solve it. This is the story of how a school student transformed concern into innovation and carried a farmer-focused environmental solution from a classroom idea to a National Level Science Exhibition.
The Problem — Why Stubble Burning Is One of India’s Biggest Environmental Challenges

After harvesting crops like rice and wheat, farmers face a difficult challenge. They must quickly clear leftover crop residue to prepare fields for the next cultivation cycle. Farmers usually have two options:

• Manually remove stubble — expensive and time-consuming
  • Burn the residue — fast but environmentally destructive

Because time and cost pressures are real, burning becomes the practical choice. However, burning releases: Carbon monoxide (CO), Nitrogen oxides (NOx), Volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and Toxic particulate matter.
Every year, this causes severe Air Quality Index (AQI) spikes, respiratory illnesses, and reduced visibility across North India.
Inspiration Behind the Project

For Ayush, this was not just a science topic. It was personal. Watching senior citizens struggle with polluted air, schools closing due to smog, and daily news discussions about parali burning made him ask one powerful question: “Instead of blaming farmers, can science help them?”

Rather than eliminating burning completely — which is economically difficult — Ayush focused on a practical middle path: Reduce pollution even if burning happens. This thinking marked the birth of the Stubble Solution Project.
The Beginning — School Science Exhibition at RPVV Yamuna Vihar

The journey began at Rajkiya Pratibha Vikas Vidyalaya, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi. Under the guidance of teacher Ashutosh Sharma, students were encouraged to participate in a science exhibition supported by major educational bodies like NCERT and SCERT.
🏆 1st Position at School Level — This victory was the first validation that their idea had real potential.
The Competitive Journey: Zonal to State Level
The journey continued through multiple levels of rigorous competition:

• Zonal Level: Facing top private and government schools. Ayush explained agricultural challenges and scientific chemistry mechanisms. ✅ Selected for Next Level.
  • District Level: At Surajmal Vihar, the intensity increased. 🏆 1st Position — District Level.
  • State Level: A test of presence of mind. Despite only 3 minutes for judging, Ayush highlighted core scientific points. 🥉 3rd Position — State Level.
National Selection — 52nd Rashtriya Bal Vaigyanik Pradarshani (RBVP) 2025

Official communication confirmed participation in the 52nd RBVP 2025, held at the Regional Institute of Education (RIE), Shyamla Hills, Bhopal from 18–23 November 2025. For Ayush Paul, this was historic — representing his school and innovation at the national level.
Technical Explanation — How the Stubble Solution Works
Part 1 — Decomposition Spray
Before burning, farmers spray a solution designed to soften stubble and partially decompose it overnight. Ingredients include:

• Ammonium Sulfate — promotes microbial growth
  • Magnesium Sulfate — activates decomposition enzymes
  • Phosphoric Acid — breaks lignin structures
  • Humic Acid — improves soil fertility
  • Cellulase Enzyme — decomposes cellulose
  • Calcium Carbonate — balances soil pH
Part 2 — Pollution Reduction Tablet

During burning, specially designed tablets reduce emissions. Key components like Calcium Oxide capture acidic gases, while Potassium Carbonate acts as a catalytic oxidant. Estimated Impact: Up to 90% reduction in harmful pollutants.
Implementation Process

1. Prepare solution mixture
  2. Spray uniformly over crop residue
  3. Leave overnight for decomposition
  4. Apply tablet powder before burning
  5. Controlled burning with reduced emissions
Challenges Faced

The journey wasn't without hurdles. Ayush had to explain complex chemistry to diverse audiences, convince skeptics that burning could be improved scientifically, and handle intense questioning under tight time constraints.
Learnings & Future Scope
Beyond medals, the biggest lesson was that innovation begins with observation. Future goals include field trials with farmers, government collaboration, and large-scale agricultural deployment.
SEO FAQ Section

What is the Stubble Solution? It is a student-developed chemical solution designed to reduce pollution emissions during crop residue burning.
Who developed it? Student researcher Ayush Paul, along with teammate Samyak Jain.
Conclusion — Innovation Begins with Responsibility
The Stubble Solution represents a mindset. When young minds observe real problems and apply science with empathy, innovation becomes powerful. 🚀 Explore more at ayushpaul.in.
